dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product asks people for a file in more places than it lists files: a layer of settings to load, a picture for a profile, a document beside a message being written. In each it offers the same thing — one button that opens the platform's own picker and, on a wide screen, a bounded place a file can also be dragged onto — and shows what was chosen in its own way. The place and its three texts are drawn alike wherever a file is asked for.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a file picker reads: the drop area's corners, paddings, gap, edge (width, dashed or solid, dash length) and glyph size; the text styles of its prompt, of the line that states the limits and of the text beside the trigger; the two gaps of the button layout; the colors of the area while a drag it can take or cannot take is over it; the timings of a state change and of a press; and, in each state, the colors of the area, its edge (also under the error condition), its glyph and its texts.
rules: A file picker keeps nothing: it hands over the files a person chose (select) and those it refused (reject), and whoever holds them shows them. For a list with rows, progress and a form's value, use the file upload, which is built from it.

The trigger is the product's own Button in the trigger slot, with the product's own words. It is the only way to choose by keyboard, by touch and with assistive technology: never ship a drop area without it.
Say the limits (kinds of file, size, count) in words with constraintsText, before the choice. accept, maxSize and maxFiles only enforce them.
Frame it with a Field for a drawn label, help, an error text and a requirement; the file picker draws none of those.
It is no form control. A form takes the file upload, or a control of the product's that holds the files.
receiving and refusing are drawn only while something is dragged over the area; error is the product's to set and stays until the product clears it.
State tokens are valued by the design system's pattern rules; the area's state-layer.color is its prompt color.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a drop zone by hand.

shape.$description: The drop area's corners: the step a card, a callout and a figure have, so the area reads as one of the form's blocks.

padding-block.$description: The room above the area's first part and below its last: what makes the area a place large enough to aim a dragged file at.

padding-inline.$description: The room at the area's start and end: the inset a card and a callout give their content.

gap.$description: The space between the area's parts: its glyph, its prompt, the trigger and the line of limits.

width.$description: The width of the area's edge, drawn inside the area's size, in every condition.

style.$description: How the area's edge is drawn. dashed: dashes and gaps of outline.dash-length, the mark of a place something can be put. solid: one unbroken line. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product has outlined cards, outlined fields and a place files are dropped on one screen, and decides once whether that place is told from the others by a broken edge or by its content alone.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A choice of kind; no dial scales it.

dash-length.$description: The length of one dash and of the gap after it while outline.style is dashed, measured along the edge. Unused while it is solid.

size.$description: The glyph at the top of the area: the largest step of the icon scale, as an empty state's.

typescale.$description: The area's prompt (dropText): the interface's running text.
The line that states the limits (constraintsText): the smallest size of text that is read, because it is read before choosing.

gap.$description: In the button layout, the space between the trigger's row and the line of limits below it.
In the button layout, the space between the trigger and the text beside it.

typescale.$description: The text beside the trigger that says what is chosen now (selectionText): running text, on the trigger's line.

receiving.$description: The area while something it can take is dragged over it. Not state tokens: nothing is hovered, pressed or disabled during a drag.

color.$description: The area's fill while it will take what is dragged over it: the quiet selection, because the area is the place now chosen.
The glyph, the prompt and the line of limits on that fill: its own content color.

refusing.$description: The area while what is dragged over it cannot be taken. The fill and the texts stay as at rest.

color.$description: The edge while the area will not take what is dragged over it: the error role, because letting go here fails.
The glyph, which becomes the icon set's block glyph, in the same role.

state-duration.$description: How long a change of the area's colors takes between states and conditions.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's). Unused by the other choices.

color.$description: The area's fill at rest: none.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: The area draws no fill at rest: its edge bounds it on whatever surface the form stands; its states draw the state layer.

color.$description: The area's edge: the boundary a person must see to find a control, as an outlined field's.
The area's glyph: secondary content, decorative.
The area's prompt: the surface's text color.
The line of limits, in both layouts: secondary content.
The text beside the trigger: secondary content, quieter than a file's name in a list.
The color hover and press mix into the area: its prompt's color.
The area's edge under the error condition: the error role. The words of the error are the Field's.
